newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank workers to protest on sick pay cuts.
newsitem.headline: German bank workers to protest on sick pay cuts.

text.p: German bank workers will on Friday stage nationwide industrial action including strikes to protest against cuts by employers in sick pay entitlements, the two main unions in the sector said on Thursday.

A joint news release issued by the HBV banking and DAG white-collar workers unions warned that thousands of workers would stop work to "raise the pressure" on banking groups to reinstitute sick pay at 100 percent of salary.

The protests are to go ahead in some 20 German towns and could involve strikes, which banking unions say the wage contracts in the sector allow them to pursue without the usual German six-week notice period.
A number of major banks, including Deutsche Bank and Dresdner Bank, have already implemented a new federal law allowing them to cut sick pay to 80 percent of workers' salaries.

Banking unions have argued that while wage contracts in the sector do not specifically cover sick pay at 100 percent of salary, the move to cut sick pay is unjustified and unnecessary because of low absenteeism in the industry.
